course_name_original: Cálculo y Diseño de Máquinas I (29103212)

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines

The student must know the different techniques for the correct design of machines and their elements, according to their working conditions and expected life, as well as the calculation and verification techniques of the product and related tests, following the different existing regulations and specifications in each case.
Have an integral vision of the functioning of machines in a mechanical assembly.
Address the design and selection of typical machine elements.
Select materials, processes and treatments for specific applications.
Present solutions for different problems in machines that may arise.
Compare different solutions for the same problem.

syllabus_topics: The design process in mechanical engineering.
Topic 6. Dimensioning of shafts and axles
Selection and life calculation of rolling element bearings.
teaching_methods: Innovative teaching activities (including open educational resources, experimental testing, and multi-subject chained practices)

assessment_methods.method: Theory and problem exam (Unique Final Evaluation)

assessment_rules: For ordinary convocation, the final grade (NC) is calculated as 35% from Exam 1, 35% from Exam 2, and 30% from Practical reports. A minimum of 4 points in Exam 1 and Exam 2, and 5 points in Practical reports are required to apply the weighted average; otherwise, NC is the minimum of these three scores. The course is passed if NC is 5 or greater and all minimums are met. For students eligible for a unique final evaluation, it consists of a theory and problem exam (70%) and a practical exam (30%), both requiring a minimum score of 5 for approval, with the theory exam also needing a minimum of 4 in each part. In extraordinary convocation (resit), students must recover failed evaluations; if a score is above the threshold but below 5, recovery is optional for compensation. All final exam grades replace previous ones and are subject to the same thresholds.
